Workflow state and process health survive a real callback restart

purpose: Exercise AC1 directly: the durable store must retain workflow_runs across a full process restart, and the freshly started process must open that store and serve requests. Assumes the driver_probe workspace DB is the canonical durable store the running callback server is bound to.

product principle: failure_recovery
rationale: The whole point of U-P5-1 is that a restart must not lose state; a fresh process reading pre-restart runs can only have gotten them from the durable store.

S3-crash-no-partial.name: generated:S3-crash-no-partial
S3-crash-no-partial.description:
Abrupt stop then restart leaves no partially applied workflow

risk: crash_mid_workflow (priority P0)
purpose: Exercise AC2 under a crash: kill the callback process (no graceful shutdown), start a fresh one, and assert the durable store holds no half-applied workflow — no orphaned audit events, no invalid state values, no duplicate live grants.
requirement: a failed write leaves no partially applied workflow
product principle: failure_recovery
rationale: A durable store must be all-or-nothing per write; an abrupt crash is the realistic way a partial write would be exposed, and the invariants below are exactly what 'no partially applied workflow' means on disk.

generated at 2026-08-10T20:30:52+00:00 (stage=initial, wave 1)
because of risk: A write interrupted by a crash commits half of a transition (state advanced but audit/ledger row missing, or vice-versa), leaving a partially applied workflow (R2), or the fresh process cannot reopen the store (R5).

S4-replay-no-reexecute.name: generated:S4-replay-no-reexecute
S4-replay-no-reexecute.description:
Restart-driven rebuild does not re-execute an effect

risk: idempotency (priority P0)
purpose: Exercise AC4: after a restart (which forces state to be rebuilt from the durable store rather than memory), the effect ledger must show no duplicated live grant for any commit_key and every CLAIMED grant must still be backed by exactly one witness — i.e. no effect was re-run on rebuild.
requirement: rebuilding state from history never re-executes an effect
product principle: outcome_verification
rationale: The dangerous failure of moving to a durable, history-backed store is that rebuilding from history re-issues an already-executed effect; the ledger uniqueness and witness 1:1 invariants are the on-disk oracle for that.

generated at 2026-08-10T20:30:52+00:00 (stage=initial, wave 1)
because of risk: Rebuilding workflow state from history after restart re-mints a grant or re-drives a committing step, creating a duplicate live effect_grants row or a CLAIMED grant with no witness (R4).

S5-rejected-writes-no-partial.name: generated:S5-rejected-writes-no-partial
S5-rejected-writes-no-partial.description:
Rejected/malformed requests create no partial workflow state

risk: malformed_input (priority P1)
purpose: Exercise AC2 from the request side: concurrent malformed callbacks (missing token, unknown path, wrong method) must be cleanly rejected and must leave the durable store with no new orphaned rows and no invalid states — a failed request is not a partial write.
requirement: a failed write leaves no partially applied workflow
product principle: failure_recovery
rationale: A failed/rejected write must leave nothing behind; firing several bad requests concurrently at the live service and then checking on-disk integrity is a cheap, executable probe of that guarantee and of concurrency safety on the reject path.

generated at 2026-08-10T20:30:52+00:00 (stage=initial, wave 1)
because of risk: A malformed or concurrent rejected request partially advances or corrupts workflow state instead of failing atomically (R2), or the server 500s instead of rejecting cleanly (R5).
